category_title: Students with SEBD who disengage due to perceived lack of opportunity in traditional settings
minimal_context: The student is in a traditional classroom setting copying trigonometry formulas from the whiteboard.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please look at the whiteboard. We are discussing trigonometry today. Copy these formulas down so we can use them to find heights.

STUDENT: (Gazes at the whiteboard and slowly starts copying) Okay.

TUTOR: Let's move on to the first example. Who can solve this on the board?

STUDENT: (Puts pen down) Usually the same four students work everything out anyway.

TUTOR: Just pay attention to what they are doing and write it down.

STUDENT: (Sits completely still like a statue, just gazing at the whiteboard) I can't keep up with the rest of the class like this.

options.A: Request that the student hand over the copied formulas, but not in an obvious or obnoxious manner.
options.B: Explain the trigonometry concepts to the student in plain and simple terms, getting straight to the point.
options.C: Use arms to block out the space of a triangle, creating a visual of what the height looks like.
options.D: Choose exploratory trigonometry activities that are neither too challenging nor too easy for the student.
